newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon t-bill auction raises 266.4 bln pounds.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon t-bill auction raises 266.4 bln pounds.

text.p: Lebanon's weekly treasury bill issue of July 3 raised 266.4 billion Lebanese pounds, according to finance ministry results issued on Monday.
The previous issue raised 253.6 billion pounds.
The issue posted a nominal surplus of subscription against maturity of 66 billion pounds. It raised the following amounts (in billion of pounds, previous week in brackets):

The central bank said seven percent of all competitive bids -- those made by Lebanese institutions -- were accepted up to the discount rate and yield for three-month bills, 20 percent for six-month bills and 60 percent for one-year bills.
The bank restricted for the first time since mid-April the acceptance of all competitive bids for the two-year bills, approving only 60 percent.

It also restricted the acceptance of non-competitive bids -- those made by private individuals and foreign investors -- for the shorter-term bills, approving seven percent up to the discount rate and yield for three-month bills and 20 percent for six-month bills.
All non-competitive bids were approved for longer-term bills.
The Lebanese pound closed at 1,539.25 to the U.S. dollar on Monday from 1,539.75 a week earlier and 1,570 a year ago.
